verdicts.claim: A normal checkpoint does not shrink the -wal file ... next writer rewinds (resets) the WAL ... overwriting an existing file is faster
verdicts.evidence: wal.html s6: 'it merely causes SQLite to start overwriting the WAL file from the beginning. This is done because it is normally faster to overwrite an existing file than to append.'

verdicts.claim: Automatic checkpoint after any COMMIT that leaves the WAL at 1000 pages or more (SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT) ... always PASSIVE
verdicts.evidence: wal_autocheckpoint.html: default 1000 or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT; auto checkpoints are PASSIVE; run after commit when WAL >= N frames.

verdicts.claim: The last connection to close also runs a final checkpoint under an exclusive lock and deletes the -wal and -shm files
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'that connection does one last checkpoint and then deletes the WAL and its associated shared-memory file'; walformat: acquires SQLITE_LOCK_EXCLUSIVE first.

verdicts.claim: PASSIVE never invokes busy handler; FULL blocks new writers not readers; RESTART waits for readers; TRUNCATE truncates -wal to zero bytes on success
verdicts.evidence: 'The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode'; FULL 'blocks new database writers ... new database readers are allowed'; TRUNCATE 'truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return'.

verdicts.claim: Every checkpoint takes exclusive WAL_CKPT_LOCK; held lock -> SQLITE_BUSY immediately without busy handler; nBackfill only increases under lock
verdicts.evidence: walformat: 'An EXCLUSIVE WAL_CKPT_LOCK is held by any connection that is running a checkpoint' and 'The nBackfill can only be increased while holding the WAL_CKPT_LOCK'.

verdicts.claim: A checkpoint must stop at the end mark of any active reader ... writer may reset WAL only when fully backfilled and no WAL_READ_LOCK(N) for N>0
verdicts.evidence: walformat: checkpoint 'must not move WAL content ... for more than the first read-mark[N] frames'; 'ok to reset the WAL if there are no locks held on any of WAL_READ_LOCK(N) for N>0'.

verdicts.claim: With synchronous=NORMAL in WAL mode, checkpoints are the only operations that fsync ... not durable across power loss; FULL adds WAL sync per commit
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'with PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, the checkpoint is the only operation to issue an I/O barrier or sync'; pragma: NORMAL commit 'might roll back following a power loss'.

verdicts.claim: If zDb is NULL or empty, sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() checkpoints every attached WAL database, continues past SQLITE_BUSY, reports it at end
verdicts.evidence: 'the operation is still attempted on any remaining attached databases and SQLITE_BUSY is returned at the end'.

verdicts.claim: SQLite 3.51.0 (2025-11-04) added PRAGMA wal_checkpoint=NOOP and SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP; NOOP checkpoints zero frames
verdicts.evidence: changes.html 3.51.0 (2025-11-04) item 7 adds the PRAGMA and SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP; v2 doc: 'This mode always checkpoints zero frames.'

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint returns (busy, log, checkpointed) ... checkpointed includes earlier frames; -1 if not WAL; 0 after TRUNCATE
verdicts.evidence: v2 doc: '(including any that were already checkpointed before the function was called)'; 'both *pnLog and *pnCkpt will be set to zero'; pragma: '-1 if there is no write-ahead log'.

verdicts.claim: Litestream maintains a read lock to prevent other processes checkpointing, asks wal_autocheckpoint=0, recommends busy_timeout 5 seconds
verdicts.evidence: 'Litestream prevents other processes from checkpointing by maintaining a read lock on the database'; busy timeout 'recommended to set this to 5 seconds'.

verdicts.claim: Litestream v0.5.x: min-checkpoint-page-count 1000, checkpoint-interval 1m, truncate-page-n 121359 (~500 MB), PASSIVE then TRUNCATE
verdicts.evidence: Page lists 1000 pages, 'Default: 1 minute', 121,359 pages '~500MB', 'Attempts a PASSIVE checkpoint first, then falls back to a TRUNCATE checkpoint'.

verdicts.claim: SQLite's 1000-page default (about 4 MB) is a compromise tested on workstations; Syncthing: multiple GB WAL grinds to a halt
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'seems to work well in test applications on workstations'; Syncthing: 'multiple gigabytes ... database operations grind to a halt'.

verdicts.claim: rqlite disables autocheckpointing and checkpoint-on-close, TRUNCATE checkpoint at each snapshot, v10 250 ms wait, salt comparison
verdicts.evidence: Post (2026-05-12): disables 'automatic checkpointing' and 'checkpoint-on-close', TRUNCATE per snapshot, 250 ms default wait, 'aborted, to be retried a few seconds later', salt comparison; dbconfig: NO_CKPT_ON_CLOSE 'zero (the default) to enable them'.

verdicts.claim: sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint() wraps sqlite3_wal_hook(), they overwrite each other; hook runs after commit with write lock released
verdicts.evidence: wal_hook: 'invoked by SQLite after the commit has taken place and the associated write-lock on the database released'; autocheckpoint 'replaces any existing callback registered using sqlite3_wal_hook()'.

verdicts.claim: The -wal file is part of persistent state ... deleting it or copying without it can lose committed transactions; safe removal = open and close
verdicts.evidence: wal.html s4: 'The WAL file is part of the persistent state ... The only safe way to remove a WAL file is to open the database file ... then immediately close'.

verdicts.claim: Three causes of unbounded WAL growth ... Since 3.11.0 a transaction writes each changed page into the WAL only once
verdicts.evidence: wal.html lists disabling autocheckpoint, checkpoint starvation, very large write transactions; 3.11.0: 'Pages ... should only be written into the WAL file once'.

verdicts.claim: Prepared statement never reset/finalized keeps transaction open; Hipp diagnosis 2021, WAL ~100 GB
verdicts.evidence: Hipp: not resetting statements 'will likely be leaving some transactions open, which will prevent the checkpoint from happening'; WAL ~100 GB.

verdicts.claim: 2021 Forum case with 36 connections and ~1000 writes/s, wal_autocheckpoint=0 on every connection made RESTART succeed; Syncthing self-contention
verdicts.evidence: '36 connections open from the same process', 'about 1000 writes per second', 'Setting PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=0; on every connection resolves the issue'; Syncthing: 'we're blocking our own checkpointer'.

verdicts.claim: New connection during close-time checkpoint fails SQLITE_BUSY; sqlite3_setlk_timeout() (3.50.0) with SQLITE_SETLK_BLOCK_ON_CONNECT waits
verdicts.evidence: setlk_timeout: new reader 'fails with an SQLITE_BUSY error'; with flag 'blocks until the exclusive lock has been released'; changes: 3.50.0 item 1 adds sqlite3_setlk_timeout().

verdicts.claim: Eaton reproduced without test hook; PASSIVE + 1 GiB mmap_size; 3.51.2 lost txn ~4s; 3.53.0 none over ~16s; integrity_check 'ok'
verdicts.evidence: 'permanently lost: 1 transactions' at ~3.5-4.3s with 'integrity_check: ok'; 3.53.0 'permanently lost: 0 transactions' real 15.946s; mmap_size 1073741824.

verdicts.claim: Tailscale manual aggressive checkpointing; corruption from Aug 2025 ~six months; Dan found and fixed 2026-03-03; integrity_check caught Tailscale corruption
verdicts.evidence: Register: 'running at our own aggressive pace', corruption detected from 'August 2025'; wal.html: 'On 2026-03-03, one of the SQLite developers (Dan) found and fixed'; Eaton: 'data corruption spotted by PRAGMA integrity_check'.
